pageData.heading: Unlocking the Power of Collateral
pageData.para: LAP (Loan Against Property) and DOD (Drop-Line Overdraft) are both credit facilities secured against property, but they serve different purposes and function differently. Here’s a detailed comparison

lap.heading: Loan Against Property (LAP)
lap.listTopPara: A term loan where you pledge your property as collateral to get a lump sum loan amount, which is repaid in fixed EMIs over a tenure.

list.heading: Lump Sum Disbursal: The entire loan amount is given at once.
Fixed EMI Payments: You repay the loan in monthly EMIs over a fixed tenure.Longer Tenure: Typically 10-20 years.
Fixed or Floating Interest Rate:Interest can be fixed or linked to market rates.

lap.listSecPara: 💡Use case : Ideal for long-term financial needs like business expansion, medical expenses, or home renovation.

dod.heading: Drop-Line Overdraft (DOD)
dod.listTopPara: A flexible overdraft facility where you can withdraw funds as needed up to a sanctioned limit, and the limit reduces over time.

list.heading: Overdraft Facility: You can withdraw money as per your requirement instead of taking a lump sum.
Interest on Used Amount: You pay interest only on the amount utilized and not on the full sanctioned limit.
Limit Reduction: The sanctioned limit reduces at regular intervals (monthly or quarterly).
Flexible Repayment: No fixed EMIs; you can repay as per your cash flow.

dod.listSecPara: 💡Use case : Best for businesses needing working capital or individuals with fluctuating cash flow needs
